title: Civic virtues
competency: Explain civic virtue and its forms: fair tax, staying informed and participating.

keywords.def: A reasoned commitment all citizens are expected to fulfil, like paying fair tax, staying informed and participating.
Not paying the tax you owe. Contraband is moving goods across the border without paying tax.

en.text: A civic virtue is a reasoned commitment every citizen is expected to fulfil for the private and public good. Examples: paying fair taxes (the more you earn, the more you pay; no tax evasion or contraband), staying informed through news, and participating in public affairs: meetings, debates, clubs, voting.

screens.ask: Why does a café give you a receipt from a cash register (Picture 1.10)?
opts: So the tax on the sale is recorded and paid
screens.after: Receipts record sales so fair tax is paid. Paying fair tax lets the government do its work.

screens.title: Civic virtue
paras: A civic virtue is a reasoned commitment that all citizens of a state are expected to fulfil.
It means citizens take part in democracy for the private and public good.

screens.title: Three civic virtues
items: Tax lets the government carry out its functions. The more you earn, the more you pay. Tax evasion and contraband hurt the economy.
Follow news on newspapers, radio and TV, so you make informed decisions.
Attend meetings, debate, join clubs and campaigns, vote, read and write about issues, serve.
